title: What If One Side of Earth Always Faced the Sun? Life Survives in a Ring

scenes.text: What if one side of Earth always faced the Sun? The survivors would all live in a ring.
The Moon already does this to us. One face, forever. Now imagine Earth doing it to the Sun. No sunrise, no sunset, no seasons, anywhere.
On the day side, the Sun hangs in the same spot for eternity. The land bakes, and the oceans get hot enough to boil.
The night side never sees light again. Its heat comes only from ocean currents and wind, and it slowly freezes under glaciers.
Between them, the temperature gap drives violent winds and endless thunderstorms, air screaming from the hot side to the cold.
Yet climate models from UC Irvine show a strip of permanent twilight that stays mild. A thin ring around the planet. That ring would be home.

description:
What if Earth were tidally locked to the Sun, with one side in permanent day and the other in permanent night? BBC Science Focus explains there would be no seasons, the day side would grow hot enough to boil water, the night side would freeze with only ocean currents and winds carrying heat, and the temperature gap would drive violent winds and thunderstorms.
Climate modelling by Ana Lobo and colleagues at the University of California, Irvine (The Astrophysical Journal) found that on such planets the day side can be scorching and the night side ice-covered, while the terminator, the thin twilight band between them, can stay habitable, forming a ring of liveable land around the planet.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The UC Irvine team found the ring works best on planets with more land than ocean; on a water world, the day side's vapour could smother the whole planet in a greenhouse. Day side or night side? Drop your own what-if below.
